urllib3 1.26.18 and 2.0.7 urllib3/util/ssl_.py both call context.load_cert_chain(certfile, keyfile) when certfile is set, mutating the supplied SSLContext; the later no-cert TLS handshake uses that same context.
findings.suggested_fix: For verify=True requests with a client certificate, use an isolated SSLContext initialized with the default CA bundle; reserve the shared preloaded context for requests without a client certificate.
findings.title: Client certificate persists on the shared TLS context
findings.why_it_matters: urllib3 loads a configured client certificate into the supplied SSLContext. Since this context is shared by every verify=True pool, a client certificate can remain on it for later requests, which may present that identity to another server; concurrent requests using different certificates can also race over the shared identity. Keeping client-certificate requests on isolated contexts prevents credentials from leaking between requests while retaining the preloaded default roots for ordinary requests.
